title: The conditions needed to maintain a current
printed_title: 87. The conditions needed to maintain a current

prose.text:
Electric current is a flow of electric charge.
Charge is a property of matter associated with electric pushes and pulls, with signs called positive and negative.
The current discussed here is conduction current, carried by charged particles moving through a material.

To produce and maintain this current, the material must contain charged particles able to move through it.
For example, a metal contains electrons that can move through the metal.
An electron is a very small particle with negative charge.

An atom is a tiny unit of a chemical element, and a molecule is a group of bonded atoms.
If opposite charges remain bound together in a neutral atom or molecule and move together, that motion does not carry a net amount of charge through the material.
Net charge means the total after positive and negative contributions are combined.
prose.source_text: **为了产生和维持电流，在物质中必须有自由的带电粒子.**如果在原子或分子中带正电和带负电的粒子束缚在一起，它们的位移不能形成电流.

prose.text:
Freely moving charged particles alone are not enough to maintain a current.
Their irregular motion can take them in many directions without a continuing net flow along the conductor.
A conductor is a material through which charge can move relatively readily.

To produce and maintain a directed motion, there must also be a force acting on the charged particles in a particular direction.
A force is a push or pull that can change motion.
Directed motion here means a continuing net movement along a direction, not that every particle follows a smooth, straight path.
prose.source_text: 但是，为了产生电流，有自由电荷还不够. **为了产生和维持带电粒子的有秩序运动，必须对它们有一定方向的作用力.**

prose.text:
An electric field describes the electric push or pull on charge at each place.
The force exerted by this field on a charged particle satisfies $\vec{F}=q\vec{E}.$

F labels the force, q is the particle's signed charge, and E labels the electric field.
An arrow above a letter indicates that direction matters as well as size.

Positive charge feels the electric force along the field direction, whereas negative charge feels it in the opposite direction.
In an ordinary conductor carrying current, an internal electric field usually produces and maintains the particles' directed motion.

Electrostatic equilibrium means that mobile charge has settled into an arrangement with no continuing directed flow.
Inside an ordinary conductor in this state, the electric field is zero.
This equilibrium statement cannot be applied to an ordinary conductor that is carrying a steady conduction current.
prose.source_text: 正如我们知道的，电场对带电粒子施以力的作用，$\vec{F}=q\vec{E}.$ 通常，正是导体内部的电场成为引起和维持带电粒子有秩序运动的原因. 只有在电荷是处于静止的情况下，导体内部的电场才等于零.

prose.text:
Potential difference is also called voltage.
It compares the energy transferred per amount of charge between two places.
Electric potential compares a place with a chosen reference, and the difference between two potentials gives their voltage.

In the ordinary conductor discussed here, the internal electric field corresponds to a potential difference between its ends.
If the conductor's condition remains unchanged and this voltage is maintained without changing over time, the current can remain steady.
Steady current means that the amount of charge passing a location per unit time remains constant.

Along the direction of conventional current through this passive conductor, electric potential decreases.
Conventional current uses the direction in which positive charge would move.

Mobile electrons in a metal drift in the opposite direction.
The following demonstration compares potentials along a conductor.
prose.source_text: 在内部有电场的导体的两端，具有电势差. 如果这个电势差不随时间改变，则在导体中有稳恒电流. 沿着通有稳恒电流的导体，电势从导体一端的最大值减小到另一端的最小值.可以用实验来显示出这个电势的减小.

prose.text:
The historical demonstration uses a damp wooden strip suspended horizontally as a conductor.
Damp wood conducts less readily than a good metal conductor, but it can still conduct charge.
The apparatus described here is not a home wiring or high-voltage handling instruction.

Metal foil leaves are attached at several places along the strip.
Their spreading angles are used to compare the sizes of electric potentials relative to the ground in this arrangement.
The angles alone do not distinguish positive potential from negative potential or supply a calibrated voltage reading.

An electrostatic generator provides the electrical supply.
An electrode is a conducting connection to the generator.

One generator electrode is connected to the ground, the reference whose potential is taken as zero.
The other is connected to an end of the wooden strip.

First, the far end of the strip is left unconnected, so the circuit has no complete conducting path.
The generator handle is turned.

Once the charge on the strip has reached equilibrium, the foil leaves spread through equal angles, as shown in Figure 167.
This indicates equal potential along the strip relative to the ground.

The strip is charged, but there is no continuing conduction current along it after equilibrium is reached.
Next, the far end is also connected to the ground while the generator continues operating.

Because the ground conducts, it completes the return path to the generator's grounded electrode.
The circuit is then closed, with a complete conducting path, and the generator maintains the current.

At the grounded end, the foil leaves do not spread: this end is approximately at the ground's potential.
The potential drop along the metal connecting conductors is small in this demonstration.
Near the generator-connected end, the leaves spread most, as shown in Figure 168.

Moving toward the grounded end, the leaves spread less.
This shows that the size of the potential relative to the ground decreases toward that end.

If the generator-connected electrode has positive potential, the signed potential also decreases toward the ground.
If that electrode has negative potential, the signed potential instead increases toward zero.

Thus the foil angles show the size of the potential relative to the ground, while the electrode's sign is needed to decide whether the signed potential rises or falls.
The potential decrease along conventional current stated earlier is consistent with either electrode sign.
prose.source_text: 取一根湿的木条作为导体，并把它水平地悬着. (这种木条，虽然不是良导体，但还是可以导电.)静电起电机作为电源. 为了看出导体上各个部分相对于地的电势，可以把一些金属箔固定在木条上. 把起电机的一个电极接地，而把第二个电极接在导体(木条)的一端. 电路是一个非闭合电路. 接动起电机的手柄. 我们发现，所有的金箔都张开相同的角度(图167). 就是说，导体上所有点对地的电势是相同的. 当电荷在导体上平衡时就应该是这样. 如果现在把木条的另外一端接地，则当旋转起电机的手柄时，情况就改变了. (因为地球是导体，所以当导体接地时，电路就变成闭合电路.)接地一端的金属箔不张开——导体这一端的电势实际上等于地面的电势(在金属导体中电势降落很小). 导体与起电机连接的那一端，金箔的张角最大(图168). 金箔的张角随着远离起电机而减小，这就证明了电势沿着导体而降落.
